The Royal Showcase event held at our college was a memorable and vibrant occasion that highlighted the creativity, talent, and teamwork of the students. The event was well-organized and reflected the spirit of hospitality and professionalism expected from students of the hotel management field.

Another highlight of the event was the teamwork and coordination among the students. Everyone performed their duties professionally, whether it was service, food preparation, hosting guests, or managing the event. Their discipline and dedication were clearly visible throughout the showcase.
The event was not only entertaining but also educational and inspiring. It gave students practical exposure to real hospitality event management and helped them gain confidence in their skills. It also allowed them to display their knowledge of food production, food and beverage service, and event organization.
Overall, the Royal Showcase was a grand success. It provided a platform for students to showcase their talent, creativity, and professional abilities. The event was enjoyable, well-managed, and left a lasting impression on everyone who attended it. Such events are very valuable for students as they help in developing practical knowledge and preparing them for the hospitality industry.

featured_reviews.name: Bavishi Alpesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Serious Concern Regarding Unethical Practices at Royal College of B.Ed. and Royal Girls School
It is extremely disheartening to witness the deteriorating ethical standards at Royal College of B.Ed. and Royal Girls School. An institution that is meant to shape future educators appears to be compromising the very principles of honesty, merit, and integrity that form the foundation of true education.
A shocking incident occurred during the Semester 1 examination in Rawal, where a B.Ed. student — who is also a staff member of Royal Girls School — was reportedly caught using unfair means (chits) during her examination. Instead of accepting accountability, she allegedly attempted to influence the situation by stating that she was a staff member of Royal College and requested special consideration.
What is even more disturbing is that despite such misconduct, she continues to be projected as an “ideal student” for others. This raises serious concerns about transparency and fairness within the institution.
There are repeated observations of favoritism due to her close association with the founder of the college. Even during lesson evaluations, where her pronunciation, explanation, and command over language were clearly inadequate, she was awarded very high grades. Such actions strongly indicate partiality rather than merit-based assessment.
When professors and institutional authorities promote such an individual as an epitome for other students, it sends a dangerous message — that influence outweighs integrity, and favoritism supersedes fairness.
This is not merely a case of bias; it is a direct attack on the values of equality, sincerity, and professional ethics. Educational institutions are expected to uphold the highest standards, especially when training future teachers. If these standards are compromised, the credibility and moral authority of the institution collapse.
Sadly, this appears to be only one among many such instances occurring within Royal College of B.Ed.
If integrity and transparency continue to be ignored, the institution risks losing the very essence of education itself.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Respected Nigar Ma’am,

I hope you are doing well. I am Hadiya, a student from the 2024–25 batch.

I am writing this with serious concern regarding the continued withholding of my original 10th Leaving Certificate (LC). At the time of my admission, you had clearly informed me that all original documents, including my 10th LC, would be returned to me after completion of my academic year. However, it has now been more than one year since I completed my 12th, and my document has still not been returned.

Recently, when I contacted the admin office, I was informed that the LC is considered “college property” and will not be returned, and that my 12th LC is “sufficient.” This statement is extremely concerning and incorrect. My 10th LC is my personal and original document, and no institution has the legal right to retain it permanently.

I would like to firmly state that, as per the guidelines issued by educational regulatory authorities such as UGC and AICTE, colleges are strictly not permitted to retain original documents of students beyond the necessary verification period. It is illegal for colleges to retain or withhold students original documents colleges are only supposed to take self attested copy of students documents. Retaining such documents without valid reason is considered an unfair and illegal practice and a violation of student rights.

This matter has now become urgent as I require my original 10th LC for my passport police verification process. Due to this delay, I am facing serious inconvenience in completing a government procedure.

Therefore, I request you to kindly take immediate action and instruct the administrative staff to release my original 10th LC without any further delay. If the document is still not provided, I will be compelled to escalate this matter formally to higher authorities, including the university, grievance redressal bodies, and concerned regulatory authorities.

I sincerely hope that such action will not be necessary and that the matter will be resolved promptly and responsibly.

Looking forward to your immediate response.

Thanking you.

Yours sincerely,
Hadiya siddiqui
(2024–25 Batch Student)
